([[Oak Forest, Illinois]]) | college = *[[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]] (2020–2022) *[[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]] (2022–2024) *[[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team1 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team2 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team3 = →Rip City Remix | highlights = }} '''Jayson Kent''' (born February 3, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley Braves]], [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State Sycamores]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. ==Early life== Kent was born on February 3, 2002, in [[Austin, Texas]].{{Cite web|url=https://bradleybraves.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jayson-kent/12539|publisher=[[Bradley Braves]]|title=Jayson Kent}} He has several family members who played [[college basketball]] or professionally, including his father Jason, mother Anna, uncles Anthony Kent and Jordan Fair, and sister Janae.{{Cite news|url=https://www.pjstar.com/story/sports/college/basketball/bradley-hoops/2022/01/12/how-basketball-means-family-bradley-rising-wing-jayson-kent-profile/9174771002/|newspaper=[[Journal Star (Peoria)|Journal Star]]|title=Why basketball means family for Bradley's late-blooming sophomore wing|author=Eminian, Dave|date=January 12, 2022}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2019/12/10/it-was-my-sisters-advice-jayson-kent-gets-shot-back-on-track-as-oak-forest-eases-past-eisenhower/|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|title=‘It was my sister’s advice’: Jayson Kent gets shot back on track as Oak Forest eases past Eisenhower |author=DiSabato, Paul|date=December 10, 2019}} At age four, his family moved to [[Chicago]], Illinois.{{Cite web|url=https://texaslonghorns.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jayson-kent/14080|publisher=[[Texas Longhorns]]|title=Jayson Kent}} Kent attended [[Oak Forest High School]] and played basketball there, initially as a [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] before switching to [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] after having a growth spurt, reaching a height of {{convert|6|ft|6|in}} at Oak Forest. He was an all-conference, all-area and all-state performer there and helped Oak Forest to the conference title as a [[Senior (education)|senior]], averaging 17.8 points and 5.5 rebounds per game. Kent posted 1,290 points and 350 rebounds in his time in high school. He committed to play college basketball for the [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley Braves]].{{Cite news|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/4/2/21204582/jayson-kent-oak-forest-bradley-basketball|newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|title=Oak Forest's Jayson Kent commits to Bradley|author=Henricksen, Joe|date=April 2, 2020}} ==College career== Kent appeared in 23 games as a [[freshman]] at Bradley in 2020–21, averaging 3.6 points and 1.1 rebounds. He became a starter as a [[sophomore]] in 2021–22, playing in 28 games while averaging 6.9 points, after which he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.pjstar.com/story/sports/college/basketball/bradley-hoops/2022/03/16/bradley-mens-basketball-player-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal/7064408001/|newspaper=[[Journal Star (Peoria)|Journal Star]]|title=Bradley men's basketball sophomore Jayson Kent enters NCAA transfer portal|author=Eminian, Dave|date=March 16, 2022}} He transferred to the [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State Sycamores]] and played two seasons for them.{{Cite news|url=https://www.tribstar.com/sports/former-sycamore-jayson-kent-signs-with-nbas-portland-trail-blazers/article_690776a0-2da7-45be-bdf0-5b4abfaec4b0.html|newspaper=[[Tribune-Star]]|title=Former Sycamore Jayson Kent signs with NBA's Portland Trail Blazers |author=Bennett, Mark|date=March 3, 2026}} Kent averaged 5.1 points per game in 2022–23, his first year with the Sycamores. He then averaged 13.5 points and 8.1 rebounds during the 2023–24 season, helping Indiana State to a record of 32–7. He helped them reach the finals of the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament]], where they lost 79–77 to the [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall Pirates]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/longhorns/article/texas-basketball-indiana-state-transfers-19776685.php|newspaper=[[Houston Chronicle]]|title=How a pair of Indiana State basketball players made their way to Austin to play for Rodney Terry|author=Bohls, Kirk|date=September 19, 2024}} He was a second-team All-[[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) selection and was named to the MVC All-Defensive team for his performance that year. Kent transferred to the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] for his final season in 2024–25.{{Cite news|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/04/14/texas-longhorns-basketball-signs-transfer-jayson-kent-indiana-state-ncaa-portal/73322717007/|newspaper=[[Austin American-Statesman]]|title=Texas basketball signs transfer Jayson Kent. What does it mean for the Longhorns?|date=April 14, 2024|author=Jones, Thomas}} He averaged 5.6 points in 27 games in his lone year with the Longhorns.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jayson-kent-1.html|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|title=Jayson Kent College Stats}} ==Professional career== Kent was not selected in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/trailblazers/onsi/news/portland-trail-blazers-sign-local-tryout-longshot-to-two-way-deal|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Blazers Sign Local Tryout Longshot to Two-Way Deal|author=Struck, Logan|date=March 3, 2026}} He attended a local tryout for the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]] and won a roster spot. He impressed with the Remix, posting an average of 11.9 points and 4.1 rebounds in his first 37 games. Afterwards, Kent was signed by the NBA's [[Portland Trail Blazers]] to a [[two-way contract]] on March 3, 2026. On March 16, he made his NBA debut against the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]], playing for three minutes and making his only shot.{{Cite
